title: Bricktop's breakfast club and the Jackson Brothers
summary: Bricktop turned the Grand Duc into an after-hours breakfast club for the smart set, with American ex-GIs the Jackson Brothers on piano and drums.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And she was — she would sing, --
She would sing, she was an entertainer.
Entertainer.
Mostly an entertainer. But, before going to -- well, should I continue with Bricktop or --
Sure.
-- should I go back to Florence's. 'Cause Florence's was before
Briggs
Bricktop's. It doesn't make any difference.
Okay. Let's finish up with Bricktop.

Well, Bricktop, she, after, several, a couple years, she was so popular that the smart set -- you see, the smart set would invade -- I say invade Montmartre, Rue Pigalle, round about 3:00 o'clock in the morning, and stay until about 8:00, 9:00 o'clock in the morning.
I see.
So she turned her place into a breakfast club, that opened around about 3:00 o'clock, and continued until 8:00, 9:00 o'clock in the morning.
So, the smart set would "Leave the different other establishments, and come and have breakfast and listen to songs -- she only had a piano player and a drums. She had the Jackson Brothers.
The Jackson Brothers?
Briggs
One playing piano and the other on drums.
These were American fellows.
Yes, yes, sure, American boys, ex-GIs from World War I, from New York.
Right.
And I believe that they were also members of the 369th.
I see, right.
